1. The Algebraic Definition

Vector ($\mathbf{v}$): An element of a vector space $V$. Think of it as an input.

Covector ($\omega$): An element of the dual space $V^*$. A covector is a linear functional. This means a covector is something that takes a vector as an input and spits out a number (a scalar).

$$\omega(\mathbf{v}) = \text{scalar}$$

In your future studies, if a vector is $v^i$, a covector is $\omega_i$. The difference in the position of the index (upper vs. lower) actually tells you which space it lives in.
